audit.why: 49.85% over 1697 games with an EVEN 6/10 rating is right, and the shape — quiet level 1, your window at 3, his window at 4-5, your spike at 6 — matches both kits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 were marked Skill in both layers while spikes[3].text calls that exact window 'his safest punish window', and 2+ items was marked Sion while whys[6] says neither side has an advantage and it splits on execution.
audit.why: The packet chart gives Levels 4-5 to Tahm Kench and 2+ items to Skill, and in both cases the page's own explanation already argued the packet's side. Abyssal Dive's 21-second rank-1 cooldown was also wrong everywhere it appeared, quoted as 12 seconds, which changes when the level-6 spike is actually cashable.
audit.corrected: Flipped two rows as matched full/content pairs — Levels 4-5 to Tahm Kench, 2+ items to Skill — with phases[3].rating dropped to 3/10 and phases[3].why restated. Corrected the 12-second figure to 21 in spikes[1].text and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tongue Lash is described as point-and-click with a slow 'into a stun you cannot dodge'. It is neither always a stun nor point-and-click, and whys[0] additionally claims it interrupts a visible charge animation.
audit.why: Riot's text: Tongue Lash damages and slows the first unit hit and applies a stack of An Acquired Taste; if the champion already has 3 stacks, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed. So the stun is a resource he has to build on you first, over a 900-range line ability, and denying the third stack removes it entirely.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[0], spikes[3].text, wants.foe[1] and mid around the three-stack requirement and the 7s rank-1 cooldown. Dropped the charge-interrupt assertion rather than reversing it.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] and late both build advice around 'Abyssal Voyage' — a global roam that does not exist on this champion — and late also calls Devour 'his W devour'.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-rework ultimate. His current W is Abyssal Dive, a short-range dive and knockup, and his R is Devour, which eats an enemy or shields an ally. He has no global ability, so 'ping it when it goes missing and use that window' is unplayable advice.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[6] and late around Devour and the absence of any global.

audit.why: Both Tongue Lash and Thick Skin heal him, and the _missing rule for this matchup is needs-antiheal. An extended trade without Grievous Wounds is one he can reset out of.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Abyssal Dive's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His window: Thick Skin absorbs your chip and Tongue Lash punishes an open charge. Farm safe, charge from fog, and count his stacks.

edits.before: His Q tongue lash is point-and-click and interrupts a visible charge animation — farm at Q-tip range and do not telegraph your charge at level 1.
edits.after: Tongue Lash hits the first unit in its 900 line and slows — the stun needs three An Acquired Taste stacks, so count them before charging in the open.

edits.before: Unstoppable Onslaught gives you a free engage threat; if he uses W (Abyssal Dive) defensively to dodge your R, his 12-second escape window is gone and you follow with a full Q-E combo.
edits.after: Unstoppable Onslaught is a free engage threat; if he spends Abyssal Dive dodging it, that is 21 seconds at rank 1 with no escape, and you follow with the full Q-E combo.

edits.before: Tahm Kench's grey-health passive absorbs your short trades and his Q tongue lash gives him a point-and-click slow into a stun you cannot dodge — this is his safest punish window.
edits.after: Thick Skin absorbs your short trades and Tongue Lash slows every 7 seconds — but the stun only fires on his third An Acquired Taste stack, so deny the third and it stays a slow.

edits.before: Neither of you has a decisive damage advantage late; it splits on execution — your passive zombie and HP wall vs his Abyssal Voyage roam. Win the side lane, track his R.
edits.after: Neither of you has a decisive damage advantage late; it splits on execution — your zombie passive and HP wall against Devour pulling a teammate out of the fight. Win the side lane.

edits.before: Force extended trades where your W-shield and max-HP passive out-last his grey-health regeneration over multiple exchanges
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds before the extended trades — Tongue Lash and Thick Skin are both healing, and time is what he needs

edits.before: Land his Q tongue lash to slow and stun you in place, then brawl while your Q charge time works against you in melee
edits.after: Build three An Acquired Taste stacks on you so the next Tongue Lash stuns instead of only slowing, then brawl

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are where he gets comfortable. His grey-health passive means every short trade he walks away with a buffer that slowly converts to real HP, and your charged Q requires him to stand still — which he does not need to do since his Q tongue lash punishes any obvious charge animation. Do not try to charge Q with him in auto range; either charge it from fog-of-war angles or hold it entirely and just farm. At level 6 the dynamic shifts back: Unstoppable Onslaught covers the gap he cannot outrun and forces him to either eat the knockup or burn Abyssal Dive to go underground. If he dives, wait the 12 seconds and go with a full Q-E; if he eats the R, the knockup immediately chains into a charged Q landing while he is grounded. Either way, your level 6 spike gives you an all-in threat he must actively spend his escape to answer.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are where he gets comfortable. Thick Skin means every short trade leaves him a buffer that converts back once he is out of combat, and your charged Q asks you to stand still — which is exactly what Tongue Lash punishes. Do not charge Q with him in auto range; charge from fog angles or hold it and farm. Count his An Acquired Taste stacks while you do: at two, the next Tongue Lash stuns; at zero it is only a slow. At level 6 the dynamic shifts back — Unstoppable Onslaught covers the gap he cannot outrun and forces him to eat the knockup or burn Abyssal Dive. That dive is 21 seconds at rank 1, so if he spends it, the window is yours for a full Q-E; if he eats the R instead, chain straight into the charged Q. Either way your level 6 is an all-in he must spend his escape to answer.

edits.before: At first item and beyond this lane is decided by who is building more purposefully — your Heartsteel HP compounding and zombie passive make you genuinely unkillable in a straight brawl, while his percent-HP damage is weak (he has none in his kit at top lane; his grey-health passive is sustain, not a damage amplifier against you). He will not kill you in a side lane duel once you have 4,000-plus HP; your W-shield alone absorbs most of what he throws out, and your passive zombie keeps trading after death. The real threat late is his Abyssal Voyage R — he can roam to save a carry or set up a pick across the map, so ping it when it goes missing and use that window to crash the wave and R-charge to an objective. In teamfights your R into the backline and his W devour of your front-line carry can both swing the fight; make sure you are the one initiating the dive, not reacting to his engage.
edits.after: At first item and beyond this lane is decided by who builds more purposefully — your Heartsteel compounding and zombie passive make you very hard to kill in a straight brawl, while Thick Skin is sustain rather than a damage amplifier against you. He will not kill you in a side-lane duel once you have 4,000-plus HP; your shield alone absorbs most of what he throws, and your passive keeps trading after death. Buy Grievous Wounds anyway: Tongue Lash heals him on every champion it touches and Thick Skin converts stored damage straight back, so a long fight without anti-heal is one he can simply reset out of. He has no global — nothing he does happens without walking there — so punish every second he spends away from the side lane. The real late threat is Devour: he eats your carry mid-fight or shields an ally out of your engage, so be the one initiating the dive rather than reacting to his.

notes: The mirror audit flagged a champion-wide defect that is bigger than this matchup: champ-data/content/tahmkench.js contains 182 occurrences of 'Abyssal Voyage' across all 71 of his matchups. That is his pre-rework ultimate and he has no global ability now, so every 'use Abyssal Voyage to teleport / apply global pressure' line on that champion is unplayable. I fixed the two occurrences that live on the sion page (whys[6] and late); the other champion needs a sweep, not per-matchup patching. Mirror findings I restated from the tahmkench side rather than re-deriving: Abyssal Dive is a telegraphed channel into a short blink and knockup, and Sion is CC-immune for the duration of Unstoppable Onslaught. I did not write the CC-immunity claim into any prose field here because it does not come from Riot's Sion text in the kit file — the mirror asserted it and I did not want to propagate it into a second page on that basis alone. It is in unverified. This full layer also carries the same mojibake as sett and shen, so I only touched clean fields.
